source_batch.unit_label: Module B unit 3 (courseware unit 12), gap closure: sexual harassment at work, the PoSH Act 2013 and the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita offences against women

facts.statement: The Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013 (the PoSH Act) defines sexual harassment as any one or more of these unwelcome acts or behaviour, whether directly or by implication: physical contact and advances; a demand or request for sexual favours; making sexually coloured remarks; showing pornography; and any other unwelcome physical, verbal or non-verbal conduct of a sexual nature. An aggrieved woman is any woman of any age, whether employed or not, who alleges she has been subjected to sexual harassment at the workplace, so the Act covers organised and unorganised sectors and domestic workers. An employee includes persons on regular, temporary, ad hoc or daily wage basis, directly or through an agent, including volunteers, trainees, contract workers, apprentices, consultants and unpaid interns.
facts.locator: WCD_POSH_HANDBOOK_2015 section 2.3; PIB_POSH_2026 (sections 2(a) and 2(f) as described)

facts.statement: Every employer constitutes an Internal Committee; enterprises that employ fewer than 10 workers, and complaints against the employer himself, fall to the Local Committee that the District Officer constitutes in each district. A complaint is made in writing to the Committee within three months of the last alleged incident. Making a false or malicious complaint or producing a forged or misleading document is an offence, but the mere inability to substantiate a complaint does not attract action against the complainant. The Supreme Court (Aureliano Fernandes v. State of Goa) directed the constitution of Internal Committees in workplaces with more than 10 employees and Local Committees at district level, and later orders (3 December 2024, 12 August 2025, 6 January 2026) directed District Officers to survey and upload details of Internal Committees on the SHe-Box portal.

The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (BNS) replaced the Indian Penal Code, 1860. Its offences against women in the chapter on criminal force and assault against a woman correspond to IPC provisions as follows: section 74, assault or use of criminal force to a woman with intent to outrage her modesty (IPC 354); section 75, sexual harassment (IPC 354A); section 76, assault or use of criminal force to a woman with intent to disrobe (IPC 354B); section 77, voyeurism (IPC 354C); section 78, stalking (IPC 354D); and section 79, word, gesture or act intended to insult the modesty of a woman (IPC 509).
facts.locator: NCRB_BNS_IPC_TABLE (corresponding section table, BNS to IPC)

facts.statement: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 came into force on 1 July 2024 (the NCRB table records that section 106(2) of the Sanhita was not to come into force on 1 July 2024).
facts.locator: NCRB_BNS_IPC_TABLE note on section 106(2); commencement notification not retrieved

payload.title: Complaints: Internal Committee, Local Committee and time limit
payload.core_explanation_md:
| Question | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| **Who handles complaints in an organisation?** | The **Internal Committee** the employer constitutes |
| **Where is there no Internal Committee?** | Enterprises with **fewer than 10 workers**, or where the complaint is against the **employer**: the **Local Committee** set up by the **District Officer** |
| **How and when to complain?** | **In writing**, within **three months** of the **last alleged incident** |
| **False complaints** | **False or malicious** complaints, or **forged or misleading documents**, are an **offence**; but **failure to prove** a complaint is **not** an offence |

**Supreme Court:** the Court directed **Internal Committees in workplaces with more than 10 employees** and **Local Committees at district level**, and later ordered **District Officers** to **survey** committees and upload details to the **SHe-Box** portal.

self_check.expected_takeaway: Within three months of the last alleged incident.

payload.title: Offences against women in the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita
payload.core_explanation_md:
The **Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (BNS)** replaced the **Indian Penal Code, 1860** (in force from **1 July 2024**).

| BNS section | Offence | Old IPC section |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **74** | Assault or criminal force to a woman with intent to **outrage her modesty** | **354** |
| **75** | **Sexual harassment** | **354A** |
| **76** | Assault or criminal force to a woman with intent to **disrobe** | **354B** |
| **77** | **Voyeurism** | **354C** |
| **78** | **Stalking** | **354D** |
| **79** | **Word, gesture or act** intended to **insult the modesty** of a woman | **509** |

The courseware refers to section 354 of the Indian Penal Code; for the position at the cut-off, read section 74 of the BNS.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: Penalties are not taught because the Sanhita text was not retrieved.

unresolved: The Act itself and the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita text on India Code were unreachable (HTTP 403 and connection refused). The PoSH facts come from a 2015 Ministry of Women and Child Development handbook and a PIB release of 6 February 2026; the BNS facts come from the NCRB corresponding section table. Penalties, ingredients of the BNS offences and the later amendment of the Act were not checked.

The Supreme Court directions reported by PIB speak of Internal Committees in workplaces with "more than 10 employees"; the handbook says the Local Committee covers enterprises with fewer than 10 workers. The items teach the Local Committee for enterprises with fewer than 10 workers and avoid the boundary case of exactly 10.

The BNS commencement date (1 July 2024) is inferred from the NCRB table note that section 106(2) was not to come into force on that date; the notification was not retrieved (fact marked needs_review).
The Hindu Succession Act 1956 (as amended) statement of the courseware and the 2016 amendment note on the PoSH Act (courseware) remain NOT taught and remain gaps.
Reviewer for this batch is the authoring agent; no independent or human review.
